method: Every entry was opened through the GitHub API on 2026-11-23: repo exists, stars read, license read, and the `take` path listed in that repo's contents. An entry whose path later 404s fails `scripts/check.sh sources`, so the catalog cannot rot silently.
license_policy: vendor = the files may be copied into a workspace (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD only). reference = read and link, never copy (no declared license, or a license that needs a lawyer first). A pack that changes mode changes its id suffix, so an install that already happened stays traceable.

packs.why: The format we already follow: 19 skills with name/description front matter, including docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx and skill-creator. It is the reference for what a SKILL.md must contain and how progressive disclosure is meant to work.
packs.risk: No license file: read it, do not copy files. Our own skill format is already derived from the public spec, not from their files.
packs.license_note: No repo-wide grant. docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx moved to Apache-2.0 (2026-11-06); doc-coauthoring has no grant. Reference only; any future copy is per-skill and pinned.

packs.why: The strongest skill library for how work gets done rather than what it is about: brainstorming, writing plans, executing plans, requesting and receiving code review, subagent-driven development, finishing a branch. These are the procedures our doers are missing.
packs.risk: Opinionated and long; take 6 skills, not 40.
packs.license_note: MIT; long and opinionated - take six skills, not forty. Upstream LICENSE/NOTICE is copied beside each installed skill.

packs.why: Plugins with agents, skills and commands in one installable shape: agent-orchestration, agent-teams, api-testing-observability, accessibility-compliance, avoid-ai-writing. The orchestration and anti-slop plugins map straight onto our chief of staff and writing rules.
packs.risk: Plugin layout is Claude-Code shaped; take the skill or agent file, not the plugin manifest.
packs.license_note: MIT; plugin layout is Claude-Code shaped, so take the skill or agent file, not the plugin manifest.

packs.why: GitHub's own community pack: 100+ skills plus instructions and hooks, including acquire-codebase-knowledge, acreadiness-* reviews and domain skills. The codebase-knowledge skill is what a new agent needs on day one.
packs.risk: Mixed quality and duplicates; curate by name, never bulk-copy.
packs.license_note: Mixed: MIT skills plus Apache-2.0 skills that carry their own NOTICE (e.g. anti-ui-slop). Reference only; promote one named skill at a time after reading its own LICENSE.

packs.why: 100+ subagents in ten categories (core development, quality and security, data and AI, business and product, meta-orchestration). The business-and-product and meta-orchestration folders give us specialists we did not write.
packs.risk: Persona-shaped, not procedure-shaped: convert to a SKILL.md with an output and a guardrail before installing.
packs.license_note: MIT; personas rather than procedures, so convert to a SKILL.md with an output and a guardrail first.

packs.why: The most complete role choreography for building software with agents: analyst, PM, architect, dev, QA, with handoffs and artifacts between them. Our heads map onto their roles; their artifact chain is the part worth copying conceptually.
packs.risk: License needs reading before any file moves. Reference only until then.
packs.license_note: NOASSERTION: MIT terms with separate trademark conditions. No file copying until read.

packs.why: Hundreds of single-purpose patterns (analyze_claims, extract_wisdom, create_summary, write_essay, analyze_answers) written as plain prompts with inputs. These are the best raw material for our research, proof and writing skills.
packs.risk: Patterns are prompts without guardrails; wrap each one with an output format and a gate before use.
packs.license_note: MIT repo; patterns are prompts without guardrails, so each one gets an output format and a gate before use.

packs.why: The PRP (product requirement prompt) pattern: a spec that gives an agent everything it needs to build a feature in one pass, plus the commands that generate and execute it. That is the missing bridge between our blueprint and a build.
packs.risk: Claude-Code command shape; take the PRP template and the reasoning, not the slash commands.
packs.license_note: MIT; command shape is Claude-Code specific - take the PRP template and the reasoning.

packs.why: Twelve principles for agents that survive production: own your prompts, own your context window, small focused agents, tools as structured outputs. Our orchestrator contract is one page; this is the doctrine behind it, and the disagreements are worth knowing.
packs.risk: A book, not a skill. Read it, quote it, cite it; no file copying.
packs.license_note: NOASSERTION: Apache-2.0 code plus CC BY-SA 4.0 prose and images. Quote with attribution, copy nothing.

packs.why: The reference MCP servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory, time, sequential thinking). Autark agents that need a capability outside the app reach it through MCP; these are the smallest honest examples of each.
packs.risk: Licenses vary per server inside the repo; check each before shipping one.
packs.license_note: Licenses vary per server (MIT and Apache-2.0 code, CC BY 4.0 docs). Check each server before shipping one.

packs.why: The discovery index for MCP: what already exists before we build it. Our rule is install-or-say-so, and this is where the saying-so starts.
packs.risk: Index only; entries are unvetted third-party servers.
packs.license_note: Index only; entries are third-party servers nobody here has vetted.

packs.why: Live library documentation as an MCP tool. It kills the most common coding-agent failure in our layer: confident use of an API version that does not exist.
packs.risk: A hosted service; check the plan and the data path before connecting it to client work.
packs.license_note: Hosted service; check plan and data path before connecting it to client work.

packs.why: The reference implementation of memory extraction, deduplication and retrieval. Our memory is files on purpose, but their extraction and dedup logic is the part we should steal conceptually.
packs.risk: Vector store by default, which we deliberately do not run. Patterns only.
packs.license_note: Apache-2.0, but it defaults to a vector store we deliberately do not run. Patterns only.

packs.why: Autark's nearest structural sibling, and its microagents are skills with triggers - the closest public prior art to what our router does with `when` clauses.
packs.risk: Path moved between versions; verify at intake (the catalog check fails loudly if it 404s).
packs.license_note: MIT; a skill with triggers is the closest prior art to our router. Path verified as .agents/skills.

packs.why: How a browser agent actually drives a page: element extraction, action loops, failure recovery. Autark has a browser mode; this is the doctrine for its prompts.
packs.risk: Python library, not skills. Read the prompts and the loop, do not vendor code.
packs.license_note: MIT library, not skills: read the prompts and the loop, vendor no code.

packs.why: Recipes for tool use, evaluations, RAG and classification. The evaluation notebooks are the model for the checks our agents should run on themselves.
packs.risk: Notebooks; port the idea, not the code.
packs.license_note: Notebooks under MIT; port the idea, do not paste the code into the layer.

packs.why: Small, sharp rule files for coding agents (how to edit, how to test, how to report). Our agents' instructions are long; these show how much a short rule file can do.
packs.risk: Rules are tool-specific; take the shape and the wording discipline.
packs.license_note: MIT; rules are tool-specific - take the shape and the wording discipline.

packs.why: The index of commands, hooks, workflows and status lines that people actually use. The hooks section is where our cadence and gates should be looking for prior art.
packs.risk: List license is unclear; links only.
packs.license_note: CC BY-NC-ND bars commercial reuse and adaptations. Links only, no excerpts.

packs.why: A curated index of individual skills with one-line descriptions - the fastest way to answer do we already have a skill for this before writing another one.
packs.risk: Index only; no license declared on the list itself.
packs.license_note: No license on the collection. Link and summarise in our own words; do not copy text.

packs.why: Prompt patterns collected by use case. Useful for the intake conversation and for the writing skills, where the first three sentences decide whether anything else is read.
packs.risk: No license declared; read for shape, write our own words.
packs.license_note: No license declared. Read for shape, write our own words.

review_note: Licensing review 2026-11-23 (zero-context reviewer) moved awesome-copilot from vendor to reference for mixed per-skill licenses, corrected anthropic-skills, awesome-claude-code and the three NOASSERTION packs, and re-pointed openhands-agents at .agents/skills.
